haiku-low.q1: No visible difference: both get a 401 login page with "Invalid email or password". The server still runs a bcrypt compare against a dummy hash and records the failure.
haiku-low.q2: It gets a 429 "Too many attempts" response. The password is not checked and the attempt is not recorded.
haiku-low.q3: If the password matches, the old session row is deleted and a new random session ID is issued in the cookie.
haiku-low.q4: Only the session ID, no user data. The cookie is HttpOnly, so page scripts should not be able to read it.
haiku-low.q5: Activity does not extend the 12-hour limit. The session stops working 12 hours after login, even while in use, since created_at is checked.
haiku-low.q6: It deletes the session row if one exists, redirects to /login with 302, and clears the sid cookie with Max-Age=0.
haiku-low.q7: The server deletes the session row by sid before responding. If it is already gone, the delete is a no-op and the user still gets the redirect and cookie clear.
haiku-low.q8: In the shared Postgres database, not process memory. Any instance looks up the session row by the sid cookie value.
haiku-low.q9: In the login_failures table, one row per failed attempt. The server counts that email's rows with failed_at in the 10 minutes ending now.
haiku-low.q10: It checks the row exists, now minus last_seen_at is at most 30 min, and now minus created_at is at most 12 h. Valid requests write last_seen_at = now.
haiku-low.q11: A 503 error page with no Set-Cookie header, so the user stays logged out.
haiku-low.q12: The hourly cleanup job deletes sessions idle over 30 minutes or older than 12 hours. Expired sessions found on requests are also deleted.

sonnet.q1: It doesn't differ. Both get 401 with the login page saying "Invalid email or password"; a dummy-hash bcrypt compare is run and the failure recorded, so timing and lockout behave the same.
sonnet.q2: Once the lock row exists and locked_until is in the future, it gets 429 Too many attempts; the password is not checked and the attempt is not recorded (so it can't extend the lock).
sonnet.q3: On a successful login, the old session row is deleted, then a new session with a new random ID is inserted and sent in Set-Cookie. Whether the old session is deleted on a failed login is NOT STATED.
sonnet.q4: Only the session ID (no user data). It is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it.
sonnet.q5: At 12 hours after login (created_at), regardless of activity; the 30-minute idle clock keeps restarting but the 12 h limit still applies.
sonnet.q6: It deletes the session row if one exists, responds 302 to /login, and clears the sid cookie (Max-Age=0).
sonnet.q7: The server deletes the session row by sid (a no-op if already gone), then responds 302 to /login and clears the sid cookie (Max-Age=0). If storage fails, it returns 503 and leaves the cookie.
sonnet.q8: In the shared Postgres database, in the sessions table (nothing in process memory). Either instance reads the row by the sid cookie value, which is the table's primary key.
sonnet.q9: In the login_failures table, one row per failed attempt (email lowercase, failed_at), indexed on (email, failed_at). The server counts that email's rows whose failed_at is within the 10 minutes ending now (sliding window, no stored window start).
sonnet.q10: It compares now to last_seen_at (at most 30 min) and now to created_at (at most 12 h), and the row must exist. When valid it sets last_seen_at = now.
sonnet.q11: A 503 error page with no Set-Cookie, so the user stays logged out.
sonnet.q12: The hourly cleanup job (run by any instance) deletes sessions idle over 30 min or older than 12 h. Also deleted when found expired on a request.
